Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE opinion no. 85 S. 02 June 2010 MR. MANUEL R. KONG 794 M. Ortiz, Barangay Washington Surigao City Dear Mr. Kong: 2m o This has reference to your earlier letter asking the Department's legal opinion relative to the passage of an ordinance providing for a supplemental budget of a province. According to you, the Sangguniang Panlalawigan approved an ordinance providing for a supplemental budget of a province. As part of the supplemental budget, a P20 million loan was included as new source of income and for the corresponding expenditures, which the treasurer and budget officer assured the sanggunian its availability as the bank has given them the assurance and has in fact submitted already all the documents required. In relation to Section 321 of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), you are now asking this Department's legal opinion on the following and we quote: "1) What does this paragraph (Section S'? I of the Local Go vernment Code) requires? 2) What the la w makers in tended when this has been drafted and discussed för enactment? S) What is the implica tion if the local treas urer wo uld not certify that the funds actually available, or in the supplemental budget itself submitted, no attachment has been made to the effect? 4) Does the logical thinking of the treasurer that the bank approved the loan by principle and submitted the bank requirement should be interpreted as FUNDS ACTUALL Y A VAILABLE even in the absence of approved loan contract from the sang-gunianP" In reply thereto, since your aforequoted queries stemmed from the passage of the Ordinance providing for the Supplemental Budget of a Province and considering further that said Ordinance has already been approved by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, we are of the view that the same should be accorded the presumption of validity unless declared otherwise by our courts of justice. Any issues or questions thereon relative to its non-compliance with the substantive requirements in the passage of a Supplemental Budget under Section 321 of the Local Government Code of 1991 should already be threshed out by filing a special civil action for Declaratory Relief before the proper court in accordance with Section 1, Rule 63 of the Revised Rules of Court, which provides that:

"SECTION 1. Who may file petition.—any person interested under a deed, will, contract or other written instrument, or whose rights are affected by a statutory executive order or regulation, or ordinance may, before breach or violation thereof, bring an action in the appropriate Regional trial Court to determine any question of construction or validity arising, and for a declaration of his rights or duties thereunder." Thank you and warm regards. Ls/17 Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: ATIV.JES B. D QUE IV Director III
